items.question: How does the approved burning of letters apply to those not yet firmly established?
premises: The burning of letters, as approved by the opponent, is beneficial in its own way.
Some practitioners have not yet attained firm establishment.
A rule that benefits the established may still apply differently to the unestablished.
items.inference: Therefore, with respect to those who have not attained firm establishment, a definite rule still holds.
items.plain_english: Thus, the burning of letters as you approve it is indeed beneficial; but for those who have not yet attained firm establishment, a definite rule certainly applies to them.

rows.grounds: demonstrative pronoun with elided initial vowel

items.question: Why does the stated mantric rule remain useful for practitioners?
premises: This mantric rule has been declared.
The rule attains practical usefulness.
Awakened mantras operate on the path of reflective awareness.
items.inference: Therefore, the mantric rule remains effective because awakened mantras function through reflective awareness.
items.plain_english: This mantric rule has been declared and it serves a real purpose, for those mantras are awakened and move along the path of reflective awareness.

items.question: How do mantras come to enter and empower the teacher?
premises: The light of consciousness is inherently autonomous.
From that autonomy, mantras are constituted of agency.
Identity with that agency can be applied to the teacher.
items.inference: Therefore, by the application of identity, agency-filled mantras enter that teacher.
items.plain_english: Because the light of consciousness is autonomous, the mantras, made of agency, enter that very teacher through the application of identity with it.

items.question: What effect do the mantras have on instruments and ritual procedures?
premises: The mantras make the teacher autonomous.
Even instruments can attain agency.
Initiation and other rites are accepted procedures.
items.inference: Therefore, through this empowerment, initiation and other accepted rites become effective.
items.plain_english: They make him autonomous, and even instruments attain agency; thus, initiation and whatever other rites are accepted become possible.

items.question: How can both injunction and prohibition be justified within this framework?
premises: Agents may perform prescribed acts or face prohibitions.
Both injunction and prohibition require a coherent basis.
In this nondual framework, all such determinations are grounded here.
items.inference: Therefore, both injunction and prohibition are established here, and all is enjoined within this very standpoint.
items.plain_english: What, indeed, is to be done by those who act, and how could there even be prohibition? Both are established right here, for all of that is enjoined here.

items.question: What happens to prohibition when viewed from the nondual path?
premises: From another standpoint, all this may appear prohibited.
A prohibition is meaningful only when clearly demonstrated.
One who rests on the nondual path sees beyond fixed oppositions.
items.inference: Therefore, once prohibition is shown in that limited way, its force is questioned for one established on the nondual path.
items.plain_english: And all this is prohibited only from that other standpoint; for when its prohibition is clearly shown, what force does it have for one who rests on the nondual path?

items.question: What remains when both injunction and prohibition are transcended?
premises: Even prohibition can be treated as an injunction from a limited standpoint.
That same prohibition can itself be negated.
Own-awareness is an overflowing ocean in itself.
items.inference: Therefore, beyond the play of injunction and prohibition, the ocean of own-awareness surges abundantly within itself.
items.plain_english: Even prohibition is enjoined, and that too is prohibited; thus the ocean of one's own awareness surges abundantly within itself.

items.question: How does this vision transform the universe and the sense of difference?
premises: The whole universe is seen as beautiful with the bliss of consciousness.
Difference appears as the opposite of that nondual bliss.
The surging of own-awareness dissolves limiting oppositions.
items.inference: Therefore, this vision reveals the universe as blissful and utterly dissolves the portion of difference opposed to it.
items.plain_english: Thus this entire universe is beautiful with the bliss of the world, and in this way it utterly dissolves the opposing element of difference.

items.question: What radiates from the knowledge-moon arising from the Supreme Lord's mouth?
premises: Knowledge is likened to a moon rising from the Supreme Lord's mouth.
That moon emits rays in all directions.
The rays shine with the mass of their own light.
items.inference: Therefore, the knowledge-moon of the Supreme Lord spreads beautiful, self-luminous rays everywhere.
items.plain_english: From the moon of knowledge risen from the mouth of the Supreme Lord, beautiful rays radiant with the fullness of their own light spread in all directions.

items.question: How is the poison affecting all beings transformed by Shiva's moon-rays?
premises: The poison called kālakūṭa afflicts the moon of all beings.
The rays of Shiva's moon fall upon it.
Mere contact with those rays melts the poison.
items.inference: Therefore, the deadly poison of all beings is transformed into an elixir by the rays of Shiva's moon.
items.plain_english: The deadly poison that darkens the moon of all beings, melted by the mere touch of the mass of rays from Shiva's moon, turns into an elixir.

items.question: What is the result of continually immersing in that transformative essence?
premises: One can plunge unceasingly into that essence.
Drinking that essence causes ecstatic reeling.
Becoming that essence removes impurity and suffering.
items.inference: Therefore, by immersing in and becoming that essence, we abide pure and freed from the threefold suffering.
items.plain_english: Plunging there unceasingly and reeling from drinking that essence, we become that essence itself and abide pure, freed from the three kinds of suffering.

items.question: What is meant by the Supreme Lord's mouth in this symbolic account?
premises: The Supreme Lord's mouth is identified with power.
That power is specifically the will.
Having arisen, that will assumes the function of the knowledge-moon in differentiated states such as Īśvara.
items.inference: Therefore, the Lord's mouth symbolizes the will-power that unfolds as the knowledge-moon across differentiated levels.
uncertainties: The exact internal analysis of īśvarādibhinnasthitivijñānaśaśāṅkaśaktivṛttam is compressed; the gloss follows the most plausible compound reading.
items.plain_english: The mouth of the Supreme Lord is said to be his power, namely will; having arisen, that will takes on the functioning of the moon of knowledge in the distinct states beginning with Īśvara.

items.question: What does the spreading mass of rays from that moon represent?
premises: From that moon a fully spread mass of rays streams forth on all sides.
The Supreme Lord possesses a power consisting of action.
That power is identified as world-pervading.
items.inference: Therefore, the mass of rays is the Supreme Lord's own action-power, which consists of the world.
items.plain_english: The fully spread mass of rays streaming forth on all sides from that moon is indeed the Supreme Lord's own power, declared to consist of action and to be made of the world.

items.question: What is the ultimate reality expressed by this expansion of powers?
premises: This reality is full of the three powers.
It expands as the supreme Bhairava.
Nothing different from it can exist, and its own expansion is called victory.
items.inference: Therefore, the supreme Bhairava alone expands as the fullness of the three powers, and nothing exists apart from that expansion.
items.plain_english: Thus this, full of the three powers, expands as the supreme Bhairava alone; nothing different from it could exist, and its own expansion is proclaimed as its victory.

items.question: How does this doctrine account for the world's conquest and multiple scriptural expressions?
premises: From that supreme reality, these powers conquer the world.
The meaning becomes manifest and fitting.
A plurality of expressions can still point to one fullness.
items.inference: Therefore, the conquest of the world and the many scriptural expressions are compatible with the one fullness of that reality.
uncertainties: The final compound vākyabhedam is syntactically compressed; taken here as the doctrine accommodating divisions of statements within fullness.
items.plain_english: From that very reality these powers clearly conquer the world; the meaning becomes manifest and fits for us, since such a connection with many expressions belongs to that fullness and accommodates the division of statements.

items.question: What does this single verse ultimately reveal?
premises: The preceding teaching can be gathered into one verse.
That verse expresses Bhairava as consciousness itself.
Bhairava contains the entire sequence of beings.
items.inference: Therefore, this single verse clearly explains Bhairava himself as consciousness, full of the entire sequence of beings.
items.plain_english: Thus this single verse clearly explains Bhairava himself, whose nature is consciousness, full of the entire sequence of all beings.

rows.grounds: emphatic particle fused with present participle

items.question: How can poison become a means to immortality in this teaching?
premises: Worldly existence is likened to poison.
Those whose vision is empowered by Garuda can use poison as medicine.
Right vision transforms what is normally harmful.
items.inference: Therefore, those established in the right vision can employ even poison and attain an immortal state.
items.plain_english: For the destruction of the poison of worldly existence, those whose vision is empowered by Garuda employ poison itself and attain an immortal state.

items.question: What is established by self-luminous awareness in this teaching?
premises: The teaching has shown its point to this extent.
Own-awareness is self-luminous.
Nothing can be established apart from that awareness.
items.inference: Therefore, self-luminous own-awareness establishes everything, and apart from it nothing at all is possible.
items.plain_english: Thus it has been shown to this extent: by self-luminous own-awareness everything is established, and apart from that nothing at all is possible.

items.question: What determines whether something is truly real in this system?
premises: Reality is measured by resting in own-awareness.
Dependence on another time undermines stable reality.
Own-awareness does not require temporal validation.
items.inference: Therefore, whatever rests in own-awareness is real, and reality cannot depend on another time.
items.plain_english: Whatever rests in own-awareness is real to that very extent; for if reality depended on another time, it could not be real anywhere.

items.question: If awareness is not bound by time, how does it relate to space and manifestation?
premises: The connection of awareness with time has been refuted at length.
Own-awareness remains the basis of manifestation.
Awareness can unfold appearances as space.
items.inference: Therefore, free from time, own-awareness functions by spreading out space in whatever way it manifests.
items.plain_english: The connection of awareness with time has been refuted at length; therefore own-awareness functions just as it spreads out space.

items.question: How is the reality of a thing tested according to this criterion?
premises: Awareness functions like a touchstone for testing appearances.
What cannot be placed upon that touchstone lacks confirmation.
Even scripture calls such a thing unreal and fit only for doubt.
items.inference: Therefore, whatever cannot be established in awareness is unreal and remains only an object of doubt.
uncertainties: The phrase saṃvidy akṣamayyāṃ is read as 'in awareness consisting of the senses/touchstone of the senses'; the metaphor is compressed.
items.plain_english: Likewise, whatever cannot be placed on the touchstone of awareness is fit only for doubt; even in scripture that is called unreal.

items.question: What distinguishes valid scripture and method from mere talk?
premises: Speech that does not ascend to own-awareness is no better than idle talk.
Scripture and method claim authority.
Only what unfolds within awareness has genuine validity.
items.inference: Therefore, scripture and method are valid only insofar as they unfold within own-awareness.
items.plain_english: What does not rise to own-awareness is no different from idle talk; that alone is scripture and that alone is method which unfolds within awareness.

items.question: Where do the world's appearances of arising and passing come from?
premises: All risings and settings of the world arise from the heart.
They are comparable to dream appearances emerging from deep sleep.
The scripture of own-awareness examines and explains them.
items.inference: Therefore, the world's cycles of arising and passing emerge from the heart of awareness, like dream from deep sleep, as understood by the scripture of own-awareness.
items.plain_english: All these risings and settings of the whole world arise from the heart, like a dream from deep sleep, and are examined by the scripture of own-awareness.

items.question: What processes make up the apparent functioning of the world in awareness?
premises: Perception depends on the totality of form, light, and attention.
Creation, maintenance, and withdrawal describe cosmic functioning.
Closing and opening, and contraction, structure the experience of beings.
items.inference: Therefore, the world's apparent operations are configurations within awareness, from perception to contraction.
items.plain_english: The totality of form, light, and attention; withdrawal, maintenance, and creation; closing and opening; and the construction of contraction in beings — all these are its operations.
